texts: good. the one-day-before-equinox anchor, Year 1, the walk with Meren as the walker, the station as destination, the station's position on the Cliff Path, and sundown are all carried, with Cliff Path named and typed.
good. a past lighting event with Meren as doer and the lantern as the thing lit, and "the station" correctly resolved back to the station of the previous sentence rather than minted anew.
good. a past burning event with the lantern as doer and mire-essence as what is consumed, and mire-essence unpacked to its essence genus.
good. the lantern carries over as the same referent, and the mist-light is given its own symbol so the next sentence can refer back to it.
good. the mist-light is the attractor and the nightmoths become a group entity later sentences can point at, with nightmoth unpacked to moth.

bad: a count noun as copular subject with a bare numeral ("the moth-count ... was seventeen") has no licensed encoding, so the translator improvised a count on a moth group and then had nowhere to put "at the third watch" or the past tense — both came out as ill-typed atoms hung on a group symbol, and the group was silently narrowed to nightmoth although your words say only "moth". Rewrite so the time has an event to attach to: "At the third watch, seventeen nightmoths were counted at the lantern." (write "moths" instead if you do not specifically mean the nightmoths of the earlier sentences). The count then rides the group, and the place, the time and the past tense all ride the counting event.

mixed: the gathering itself is clean — a nightmoth group with "a handful" recorded as stated, a collective gather event, the Middle Row named and typed, past tense. But "that night" resolves only to a bare night-of-day marker with no day attached, so nothing ties it to Meren's walk or to the sky-cats' night. Rewrite as "A handful of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row that night, one day before the autumn equinox of Year 1." so the night is back on the calendar.

bad: staying is something each cat does separately, but the parse records only one group-level stay event with no per-member rule, so a sky-cat named later is not derivably one that stayed; and "that night" again lands as a bare night with no day attached, unlinked to Meren's walk or to the moths' gathering. Rewrite as "All the sky-cats stayed on the cliff-spires that night, one day before the autumn equinox of Year 1." — the explicit universal forces the per-member distribution, and the restated anchor puts the night back on the calendar.
